wins.label: Strong Data Center Growth
wins.evidence: Data Center segment revenue increased 115% year-over-year to a record $2.8 billion driven by the steep ramp of Instinct MI300 GPU shipments.

wins.label: EPYC Adoption Expansion
wins.evidence: Hyperscalers select EPYC processors to power a larger portion of their applications and workloads, displacing incumbent offerings across their infrastructure.

wins.label: AI Software Ecosystem Growth
wins.evidence: AMD support for FlashAttention-2 algorithm was upstreamed, providing out-of-the-box support for AMD hardware in the popular library.

wins.label: Next-Gen Product Roadmap
wins.evidence: We plan to follow MI325X with the MI350 series in 2025 based on the new CDNA 4 architecture, which is on track to deliver a 35x increase in performance compared to CDNA 3.

wins.label: Client Segment Growth
wins.evidence: Client segment revenue was $1.5 billion, an increase of 49% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for our prior generation Ryzen processors.

risks.label: Gaming Segment Decline
risks.evidence: Gaming segment revenue declined 59% year-over-year to $648 million as semi-custom SoC sales declined in line with our projections.

risks.label: Embedded Segment Recovery
risks.evidence: Embedded segment revenue decreased 41% year-over-year to $861 million, with recovery expected to be gradual in the second half of the year.

risks.label: Supply Chain Constraints
risks.evidence: The overall supply chain is tight and will remain tight through 2025, which may impact the ability to scale production of MI300 and future products.

risks.label: Competitive Pressure
risks.evidence: There is ongoing industry debate about AI monetization and whether customers are getting the right ROI on their CapEx, which may lead to consolidation around other suppliers.

risks.label: Software Adoption Challenges
risks.evidence: There are challenges in ramping the next wave of customers, particularly in terms of software optimization and integration with AMD hardware.
